questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Language that I already knew some of and a desire to be better at it. 
Culture that I found interesting
City that I had heard was interesting

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. The exchange office at the Health department at Sorbonne university were very quick at answering and kind to help. The hospital department wrote to me a few weeks before so I knew where and when to go

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: An intro meeting with the person in charge of my exchange at the hospital during the first week. I wished I had a bit more information before starting. I was not aware of the requriements for my exchange and the first two days the only ones that could guide me, where other (local) students that did not know much about my exchange

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It could have been made clear that I, as an exchange student, was supposed to participate in the same way as the local students. They planned their entire clinical stay on the first day and did not include me unless they needed a hole in the schedule to be filled. I was not aware of what I could/should do and therefor I had very few days planned. For the first six weeks I (most days) had to figure out what to do day to day, and find out what was available.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
The Cite Universitaire (CIUP) is a really awesome place to stay. Especially Fondation Danoise 
Very easy to apply and I of course got accepted. I do not know how many people they turn away

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Go to CIUP and stay - it is easy and affordable and a really cool place

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I do not remember much, since it was over a year ago. I do remember that there were many odd things I had to fill out that I did not really understand. Luckily I wrote with a student that had been on exchange at the same place earlier, who could guide me a bit

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very. I got my first priority. Maybe I would have liked to have been to two different departments, as 13 weeks in the same department is a very long time. But I had no idea how to make it clear that I wanted to split my time in two.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not take all the tiny things in the application process to serious. If there is something you filled out wrong they will contact you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Clinical rotation, similar to the Danish ones in many ways.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot of the same.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Clinical rotation in Gynecology and Obstetrics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Clinical rotation in Gynecology and Obstetrics - only one I had...

questions.answer: I ended up taking French lessons, arranged by the Danish church in Paris

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were a bit more expensive than expected - though much cheaper on the outdoor markets that happened a few times a week. The bakeries were very cheap :)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Did not use any

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I do not know, I was never informed of any.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
French lessons at the Danish Church 
Sport at the Cite Universitare

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the Garnier Opera and get cheap nosebleed tickets on the same day

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. I recommend following French/Parisian people and sites on instagram. Especially foreigners who have moved to Paris - they have a good insight in to the culture and are very good at explaining little differences that the French do not necessarily know about

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The politeness - you say hello to everyone. 
Bakeries - they are everywhere, cheap and almost always fantastic

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Do not expect people to know more than two words of English. 
Be active - even if there is a language barrier, most people are very friendly and would like for you to learn

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My French have gotten a LOT better, even though I am no where near fluent. I got to experience a medical speciality I am very interested in and got more sure of my future carreer.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Language

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
